newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines plans to import up to 300,000 T corn.
newsitem.headline: Philippines plans to import up to 300,000 T corn.

text.p: The Philippines plans to import between 250,000 tonnes and 300,000 tonnes of corn to meet the needs of local livestock farmers next year, Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero told reporters on Wednesday.
"We are planning to request (President Fidel Ramos) to approve the importation of between 250,000 tonnes and 300,000 tonnes of corn for the first quarter of 1997," Escudero said.
The Department of Agriculture will submit the request within the week, he said.
Escudero said local farmers had estimated the total corn import requirment for 1997 could go up to 600,000 tonnes.
"We are inclined to (request) for 250,000 tonnes to 300,000 tonnes although it is always subject to review," Escudero said.
"We don't want it (local corn shortfall) to be a constraint to the further expansion of livestock industry," he said.
Escudero said his department was looking at the United States and Argentina as possible sources for the country's corn requirement.
The Philippines has imported 400,000 tonnes of corn from both countries since the start of the year.
